payload.stem: A least-squares line $\hat y = 30 - 2.2x$ predicts its resale value in thousand dollars from the age of a car in years, using data with $x$ from $2$ to $10$ years and a strong linear association. A researcher considers predictions for $x = 8$, $x = 12$, $x = 22$ and $x = 1$. Which prediction is the most reliable, and why?

options.text: The prediction for $x = 12$, because it is only a little beyond the largest value of $x$ in the data.
options.why: $12$ is outside the range of the data ($2$ to $10$), so the prediction is an extrapolation, even though it is close to the range.

options.text: The prediction for $x = 8$, because $8$ is between the smallest and the largest values of $x$ in the data.
options.why: The data have values of $x$ from $2$ to $10$, and a prediction inside that range is an interpolation, which is the most reliable kind.

options.text: The prediction for $x = 1$, because the linear association is strong.
options.why: $1$ is below the smallest value of $x$ in the data, and a strong correlation within the range does not make predictions outside it reliable.

options.text: The prediction for $x = 22$, because the line is a least-squares line that fits all of the data.
options.why: A good fit within the range of the data does not show that the line continues to hold far outside the range.
